chapters.title: 1. 아버지라고 부를 수 없는 아이
chapters.text:
옛날에 홍 판서라는 사람이 있었습니다. 홍 판서는 나라에서 높은 벼슬에 있었습니다. 나라에서 중요한 일을 했고, 많은 사람들이 그를 잘 알았습니다.

홍 판서에게는 두 아들이 있었습니다. 첫째 아들은 홍인형이었습니다. 인형의 어머니는 유 부인이었습니다. 유 부인은 홍 판서의 아내였습니다. 둘째 아들은 홍길동이었습니다. 길동의 어머니는 춘섬이었습니다.

춘섬은 처음에 홍 판서의 집에서 일하는 사람이었습니다. 나중에는 홍 판서와 함께 살게 되었습니다. 그리고 길동이 태어났습니다. 홍 판서는 아들을 보고 기분이 아주 좋았습니다. 하지만 길동의 어머니가 유 부인이 아니라서 마음이 아프기도 했습니다.

길동은 여덟 살이 되었습니다. 공부를 아주 잘했습니다. 하나를 배우면 다른 것도 많이 알 수 있었습니다. 홍 판서는 길동을 더 많이 사랑했습니다.

하지만 길동은 형과 똑같이 살 수 없었습니다. 춘섬은 집에서 일하는 사람이었고, 사람들은 춘섬을 중요한 사람으로 생각하지 않았습니다. 사람들은 춘섬의 아들인 길동도 중요한 사람으로 생각하지 않았습니다. 길동이 홍 판서를 ‘아버지’라고 부르면 홍 판서는 화를 냈습니다. 인형을 ‘형’이라고 불러도 화를 냈습니다.

길동은 이제 열 살보다 나이가 많았습니다. 하지만 아버지를 ‘아버지’라고 부를 수 없었습니다. 형을 ‘형’이라고 부를 수도 없었습니다. 그 집에서 일하는 다른 사람들도 길동을 중요한 사람으로 생각하지 않았습니다. 길동은 마음이 매우 아팠습니다.

어느 가을 밤이었습니다. 달이 밝았습니다. 길동은 책을 읽고 있었습니다. 그리고 더 읽지 않고 말했습니다.

“나는 나라를 돕고 큰 일을 하고 싶다. 그런데 왜 이렇게 혼자인 것 같을까? 나에게도 아버지가 있다. 형도 있다. 하지만 아버지를 아버지라고 부를 수 없다. 형을 형이라고 부를 수도 없다. 정말 마음이 아프다.”

길동은 집 밖으로 나갔습니다. 그리고 칼을 가지고 싸우는 연습을 했습니다. 홍 판서도 밖에서 달을 보고 있었습니다. 길동을 보고 불렀습니다.

“밤이 늦었는데 왜 아직 안 자니?”

길동은 대답했습니다.

“달이 좋아서 보고 있었습니다. 다른 사람들은 모두 중요한 사람입니다. 그런데 저는 그렇지 않습니다. 저도 사람인데, 왜 저는 다른 사람들과 다릅니까?”

홍 판서는 길동의 말을 이해했습니다. 그런데도 화를 내며 물었습니다.

“그게 무슨 말이냐?”

길동이 다시 말했습니다.

“저는 아버지의 아들입니다. 아버지와 어머니께 감사합니다. 하지만 저는 아버지를 ‘아버지’라고 부를 수 없습니다. 형을 ‘형’이라고 부를 수도 없습니다. 그래서 항상 슬픕니다.”

길동은 울었습니다. 홍 판서도 마음이 아팠습니다. 하지만 길동에게 좋은 말을 해 주면, 길동이 아버지의 말을 듣지 않을까 걱정했습니다. 그래서 길동에게 크게 화를 냈습니다.

“높은 벼슬을 하는 사람의 집에서 일하는 여자의 아들은 너만 있는 것이 아니다. 왜 너는 이런 말을 하느냐? 다시 이런 말을 하면 내 앞에 올 수 없다.”

길동은 아무 말도 할 수 없었습니다. 아버지 앞에서 계속 울었습니다.

“이제 돌아가라.”

홍 판서의 말을 듣고 길동은 방으로 돌아갔습니다. 방에서도 길동의 마음은 계속 슬펐습니다.

segments.story_importance_en: The official post establishes the high status of the household whose servant's son faces unequal treatment.

segments.meaning_en: words like this (as the object of saying)

grammar_links.context_en: 에 marks 옛날 as the time when the story takes place.
라는 connects 홍 판서 to the following noun 사람: a person called Minister Hong.
이 marks 사람 as the subject whose existence is introduced by 있었습니다.
-었- places this person's existence in the past: there was a person.
-습니다 ends the past statement in the narrator's formal polite style.
는 makes Minister Hong the topic of the statement about his government position.
에서 identifies the country as the setting in which Minister Hong held his official position.
높은 describes 벼슬 as high-ranking. Its written form is 높은; its pronunciation is 노픈.
에 marks the official position occupied by Minister Hong; 벼슬에 있다 means to hold a government post.
The past form places Minister Hong's holding of the post in the story's past.
습니다 gives the narrator's statement its formal polite ending.
에서 marks the country as the setting of Minister Hong's important work in government.
중요한 describes the following noun 일: important work.
을 marks 일 as the work Minister Hong did.
했- places his work in the past; 하였- contracts to 했-.
고 connects his doing important work with the statement that many people knew him.
많은 describes 사람들이: many people.
들 makes 사람 explicitly plural: people.
이 marks 사람들이 as the people who knew Minister Hong.
를 marks 그, referring to Minister Hong, as the person they knew.
았 places people's knowing him in the past.
습니다 ends the narrator's statement in a formal polite style.
With 있다, 에게 marks the person who has something or stands in the stated relationship: Minister Hong had two sons.
는 follows 에게 to make Minister Hong the topic of the statement about his sons.
이 marks 아들 as the subject of 있다; with 홍 판서에게, the sentence expresses that Minister Hong had two sons.
있었다 places the existence of his two sons in the past; the whole sentence means that Minister Hong had two sons.
-습니다 completes the past predicate as a formal polite narrative statement.
은 marks the first son as the topic: the sentence identifies him as Hong Inhyeong.
이다 identifies the first son as Hong Inhyeong.
The past form presents this identification within the story's past-time narration.
습니다 ends the identification in the narrator's formal polite style.
의 connects Inhyeong to his mother: ‘Inhyeong’s mother’.
는 marks Inhyeong’s mother as the topic; the sentence identifies her as Lady Yu.
이다 identifies Inhyeong’s mother as Lady Yu.
The past form 이었- places this identification in the story’s past.
-습니다 gives the narrator’s statement a formal polite ending.
은 marks Lady Yu as the person this statement is about.
의 connects Minister Hong to 아내: Lady Yu was his wife.
The copula identifies Lady Yu as Minister Hong’s wife.
The past form places this relationship in the time of the story.
-습니다 ends the narrator’s statement in a formal polite style.
은 marks the second son as the topic, contrasting him with the first son introduced earlier.
The copula identifies the second son as Hong Gildong.
The past form presents this identification within the story's past-time narration.
-습니다 closes the sentence in the narrator's formal polite style.
의 connects Gildong to his mother: Gildong's mother.
는 makes Gildong's mother the topic; the sentence identifies her as Chunseom.
The copula connects Gildong's mother with her identity, Chunseom.
The past form identifies Chunseom as Gildong's mother in the past-time narrative.
-습니다 ends the narrator's statement in a formal polite style.
은 introduces Chunseom as the person this sentence describes.
에 marks the initial period: Chunseom initially worked in the household.
의 connects Minister Hong to his household.
에서 marks Minister Hong's household as the place where Chunseom worked.
일하는 describes 사람 as someone who works. Here the work belongs to the past period established by 사람이었습니다.
The copula identifies Chunseom as a person who worked in Minister Hong's household.
었 places Chunseom's initial role in the past.
습니다 closes the narrator's statement in a formal polite style.
에 marks 나중 as the time when Chunseom's situation changed: later.
는 contrasts her later situation with her initial work in the household.
와 identifies Minister Hong as the person Chunseom came to live with.
-게 links 살다 to 되다, presenting living together as the situation that came about.
살게 되었습니다 describes a change in Chunseom's circumstances: she came to live with Minister Hong.
-었- places the change in her living situation in the past.
-습니다 gives the past statement the narrator's formal polite style.
이 marks Gildong as the person who was born.
-았- places Gildong's birth in the past; 태어나 plus -았- contracts to 태어났-.
-습니다 gives the statement a formal polite ending.
는 makes Minister Hong the topic: the sentence describes his response to seeing his son.
을 marks his son as the person Minister Hong saw.
-고 connects seeing his son with feeling happy. The final past ending places both in the past.
이 marks 기분 as the subject of 좋았습니다. 기분이 좋다 means to feel good or happy; here Minister Hong felt very happy.
-았- places Minister Hong's good mood in the past.
-습니다 closes the narrator's statement in a formal polite style.
의 connects Gildong to his mother. 길동 is the approved shortened form of 홍길동.
가 marks Gildong’s mother as the subject of the statement that she was not Lady Yu.
이 marks Lady Yu as the identity denied by 아니다: Gildong’s mother was not Lady Yu.
아니다 takes the form 아니라서 to give the reason for Minister Hong’s emotional pain. The past setting comes from the surrounding narrative and final predicate.
이 marks 마음 as the subject of 아프다. Here 마음이 아프다 means to feel emotional pain.
기 turns 아프다 into a nominalized state within the construction -기도 하다.
도 adds emotional pain to Minister Hong’s happiness described in the preceding sentence.
아프기도 하다 expresses that he also felt hurt, alongside his happiness about his son.
했다 places this additional feeling in the past.
했습니다 ends the narrator’s statement in the formal polite style used throughout the chapter.
은 identifies Gildong as the person whose age is being described.
이 marks 여덟 살, ‘eight years old,’ as the age complement of 되다: the age Gildong reached.
-었- places Gildong’s turning eight in the past.
-습니다 ends the narrator’s statement in a formal polite style.
를 marks 공부 as the activity Gildong did well at: he was very good at his studies.
The past form describes how well Gildong studied at this point in the story.
습니다 ends the narrator's statement in a formal, polite style.
를 marks the one thing Gildong learned.
면 introduces the condition: if Gildong learned one thing, he could understand many other things. The final past predicate places this ability in the past.
도 adds other things to the one thing he learned; 다른 것도 means 'other things too'.
알 is the modifier form of 알다 before 수. The stem already ends in ㄹ, so the resulting form is 알.
알 수 있었습니다 expresses Gildong's ability to know or understand things in the past.
었 places the possibility expressed by 있다 in the past.
습니다 ends the narrator's statement in a formal polite style.
는 marks Minister Hong as the topic: the sentence describes his growing love for Gildong.
을 marks Gildong as the person Minister Hong loved.
The past form 사랑했다 expresses that Minister Hong loved Gildong even more.
습니다 ends the past statement in the narrator's formal polite style.
은 makes Gildong the topic, contrasting his restricted life with his older brother's.
과 marks his older brother as the person with whom Gildong's way of living is compared through 똑같이.
살 is the modifier form of 살다 before 수. Because the stem already ends in ㄹ, no additional ㄹ is written.
살 수 없었습니다 expresses that Gildong's circumstances prevented him from living the same way as his older brother.
-었- places the lack of possibility in the past.
-습니다 gives the past statement the chapter's formal polite narrative style.
은 introduces Chunseom as the topic of the statement about her work in the household.
에서 marks the household as the place where Chunseom worked.
일하는 describes 사람: a person who worked in the household. The main predicate places this description in the past.
The copula connects Chunseom with the description 집에서 일하는 사람, a person who worked in the household.
이었 places Chunseom's household role in the past.
고 connects the statement about Chunseom's work with the statement about how people regarded her.
들 makes 사람 plural: people.
은 introduces people as the topic of the statement about their judgment of Chunseom.
을 marks Chunseom as the person whom people judged.
중요한 modifies 사람, meaning an important person.
으로 marks the category in which Chunseom is considered: an important person. The following negation says people did not regard her this way.
지 connects 생각하다 to the negative auxiliary 않다.
생각하지 않았습니다 negates the act of regarding Chunseom as an important person and places it in the past.
았 places the negative judgment in the past: people did not regard her as important.
습니다 ends the negative statement in the narrator's formal polite style.
들 makes 사람 plural: the people who treated Chunseom and Gildong as unimportant.
은 marks 사람들 as the topic: what these people thought about Gildong.
의 connects Chunseom to her son; 춘섬의 아들 means ‘Chunseom’s son’.
The copula connects the following person, Gildong, with the identity ‘son’.
인 makes 아들 describe 길동: Gildong, who is Chunseom’s son.
도 includes Gildong in the same dismissive treatment already given to his mother: Gildong too.
중요한 describes the following 사람: an important person.
으로 marks the category in which someone is regarded. 중요한 사람으로 생각하다 means ‘regard someone as an important person’.
지 connects 생각하다 to the negative auxiliary 않다.
지 않다 negates regarding Gildong as an important person; the final auxiliary carries past time and formal politeness.
았 places the negative statement in the past: these people did not regard Gildong as important.
습니다 gives the narrator’s negative past statement a formal polite ending.
이 marks Gildong as the person calling Minister Hong “Father.”
를 marks Minister Hong as the person Gildong addresses.
라고 marks “Father” as the title Gildong uses to address Minister Hong.
-면 gives the condition that triggers Minister Hong's anger. In this past narrative, it describes what happened whenever Gildong called him “Father.”
는 introduces Minister Hong as the topic of the response to Gildong's address.
를 marks 화 as the object in the expression 화를 내다, meaning to get angry or show anger.
내다 becomes 냈다 in the past. Here 화를 냈다 means that Minister Hong got angry.
-습니다 makes the past statement 냈습니다 formal and polite; it is the narrator's style.
을 marks Inhyeong as the person Gildong calls ‘older brother’.
이라고 marks ‘형’ as the title Gildong uses for Inhyeong.
Calling Inhyeong ‘older brother’ also provoked Minister Hong's anger. 부르다 forms 불러 through 르-irregular conjugation, and -도 completes the concessive form 불러도, ‘even if he called him’.
를 marks 화 as the object in the idiomatic expression 화를 내다, ‘get angry’.
내다 takes the past ending -었-, with 내었- contracting to 냈-. In 화를 냈다, the complete expression means ‘got angry’.
-습니다 follows the past stem 냈- to form 냈습니다, giving the narrator's statement a formal polite ending.
은 makes Gildong the topic: the sentence describes his age at this point in the story.
살 counts years of age, and 보다 marks the comparison point. The preceding 열 supplies ten, so 열 살보다 means ‘than ten years old’. With 나이가 많았습니다, this says that Gildong was older than ten.
가 marks 나이, age, as the subject of 많았습니다. His age was greater than ten years.
-았- places the description of Gildong's age in the past: he was older than ten.
-습니다 closes the narrator's statement in the formal polite style.
를 marks the father as the person Gildong could not address by the title “Father.”
라고 marks “Father” as the quoted title used with 부르다, “to call.”
부를 modifies 수, presenting calling someone as a possible action.
부를 수 없었습니다 says that Gildong could not address his father as “Father.” Here the restriction comes from his circumstances.
었 places the lack of possibility in the past.
습니다 ends the narration in a formal polite style.
을 marks the older brother as the person Gildong could not address by this title.
이라고 marks ‘형’ as the title used when addressing his older brother.
부를 modifies 수; together with 없다, it expresses being unable to call someone by a title.
The construction expresses that Gildong was unable to address his older brother as ‘Brother’. 도 adds this restriction to the preceding restriction concerning his father.
grammar_links.display_meaning_en: could not even call him that

grammar_links.context_en: 도 adds another restriction: Gildong could not call his older brother ‘Brother’ either.
The past ending places this restriction in the time of the narrative.
습니다 closes the narrator’s statement in a formal polite style.
에서 marks the household as the place where the people worked.
일하는 describes the people as working in that household; the surrounding past narrative supplies the time.
들 explicitly marks 사람 as plural: the other people working in the household.
도 means that these other household workers also failed to regard Gildong as important.
을 marks Gildong as the person whom the workers judged.
중요한 describes 사람: an important person.
으로 marks the category in which Gildong was considered: an important person.
-지 connects 생각하다 to the negative auxiliary 않다 that follows.
생각하지 않았습니다 denies that the workers regarded Gildong as an important person.
-았- places the workers' negative judgment in the past.
-습니다 closes the negative past statement in the narrator's formal polite style.
은 establishes Gildong as the person whose feelings are described.
이 marks 마음 as the subject of 아팠습니다. Here 마음이 아프다 expresses emotional pain.
The past form 아팠다 describes the emotional pain Gildong felt at this point in the story.
-습니다 ends the past statement in the narration's formal polite style.
The copula identifies the time of the scene as a night; 이 is part of the copula here.
The past form places this autumn night in the story's past.
The narrator ends the statement in the formal polite style.
이 marks the moon as the subject of the description.
-았- places the moon's brightness in the past.
-습니다 ends the description in the narration's formal polite style.
은 introduces Gildong as the person the sentence is about.
을 marks the book as what Gildong was reading.
Here -고 links 읽다 to the progressive auxiliary 있다 to describe ongoing reading.
읽고 있었습니다 describes reading that was in progress at that past moment.
-었- places the ongoing reading in the past.
-습니다 gives the narration a formal polite ending.
-지 connects 읽다 to the negative auxiliary 않다.
읽지 않고 says that he did not read further and then spoke. 더 supplies ‘any more’; the final predicate supplies the past narrative time.
-고 connects not reading further with speaking. 말했습니다 establishes past time for both actions.
말하다 becomes 말했다 to place his speaking in the past.
-습니다 gives the past statement the narrator’s formal polite style.
는 marks Gildong's 'I' as the topic of his statement.
를 marks the country as what Gildong wants to help.

-고 connects helping the country with doing great deeds; both actions fall under his wish expressed by 싶다. 돕고 is pronounced [돕꼬]: ㄱ becomes tense after the final ㅂ sound, while the written form remains 돕고.
큰 describes the following 일을: great deeds or significant accomplishments. Its pronunciation is [큰], matching its spelling.
을 marks the deeds as what Gildong wants to do.
하고 is the -고 form of 하다 used before 싶다 to express wanting to do something. Its pronunciation is [하고], matching its spelling.
하고 싶다 expresses Gildong's wish to do great deeds. The earlier connected action, helping the country, is also part of this wish.
-다 ends 싶다 as a plain statement of desire: Gildong says to himself that he wants to help the country and do great deeds.
이렇- + -게 forms the written form 이렇게, retaining the stem-final ㅎ. In pronunciation, ㅎ and the following ㄱ combine as aspirated ㅋ, giving [이러케]. Here 이렇게 means ‘so’ in ‘Why do I feel so alone?’
The copula combines with 혼자 to express being alone. 혼자이다 is pronounced [혼자이다].
혼자인 modifies 것, presenting being alone as the situation the speaker is considering. 혼자인 is pronounced [혼자인].
혼자인 것 같다 expresses the speaker's feeling or impression of being alone. Together with 왜 이렇게 and the questioning ending, the sentence means ‘But why do I feel so alone?’

The speaker asks himself why he feels this way. -(으)ㄹ까 marks a question considered inwardly. 같- + -을까 is written 같을까 and pronounced [가틀까]: the stem-final ㅌ is pronounced at the start of the following vowel-initial syllable.
With 있다, 에게 marks the person who has something or a relationship. 나에게 아버지가 있다 means ‘I have a father.’
도 adds ‘too’ to the person marked by 에게: ‘I too have a father.’
가 marks 아버지 as the subject of 있다, identifying the family relationship the speaker has.
The plain statement ending -다 suits Gildong’s words to himself. The sentence means ‘I too have a father.’
도 adds an older brother to the father already mentioned: Gildong has an older brother too.
있다 ends this statement in a plain style appropriate to Gildong's private thoughts. The understood possessor is Gildong: 'I have an older brother too.'
를 marks the father as the person whom Gildong cannot call by the title ‘Father’.
라고 marks 아버지 as the title ‘Father’ used with 부르다, ‘to call’.
부르다 becomes 부를 before 수 to describe the action whose possibility is being denied. 부를 is pronounced 부를, as written.
부를 수 없다 means ‘cannot call’; here Gildong is forbidden to address his father as ‘Father’.
-다 ends 없다 as a plain statement in Gildong’s speech: calling his father ‘Father’ is not possible. Here 없다 is a complete predicate, with the same written form as its dictionary headword.
을 marks the older brother as the person Gildong cannot address by that title.
이라고 marks ‘older brother’ as the title used with 부르다, ‘call’.
부를 places the action ‘call’ before 수 to discuss whether it is possible. Its pronunciation is 부를, matching the written form.
부를 수 없다 denies the possibility of calling him that. 도 adds that this restriction applies to his brother too.
도 adds another denied possibility: Gildong cannot call his brother ‘older brother’ either, just as he cannot call his father ‘father’.
The ending -다 in 없다 closes Gildong’s plain, non-polite statement that calling his brother ‘older brother’ is not possible either.
이 marks 마음 as what hurts. 마음이 아프다 expresses emotional pain: Gildong feels hurt and sad.
The descriptive predicate ends in plain -다 as Gildong expresses his feelings to himself.
은 marks Gildong as the topic: the sentence tells what he did.
으로 marks the direction of movement; 집 밖으로 means outside the house.
나가다 becomes 나갔다, placing Gildong's movement in the past.
나갔습니다 reports that he went out in the narrator's formal polite style.
을 marks the sword as what Gildong holds and uses.
-고 connects holding the sword with the fighting practice that follows: he practices with the sword.
싸우는 describes 연습: practice in fighting. The modifier does not place the practice in the present; the final verb sets the past time.
을 marks practice as the activity he did; 연습을 하다 means to practice.
하였- contracts to 했-, placing his practice in the past.
-습니다 gives the narrator's statement a formal polite ending.
도 adds Minister Hong: he too was outside looking at the moon.
에서 marks outside as the place where Minister Hong was looking at the moon.
을 marks the moon as what Minister Hong was looking at.
-고 connects 보다 to the progressive auxiliary 있다, forming an ongoing action here.
보고 있었습니다 says that looking was already in progress at this point in the story.
-었- places the ongoing action of looking in the past.
-습니다 gives the narrator's statement its formal polite ending.
을 marks Gildong as the person Minister Hong sees and calls to.
-고 connects seeing Gildong with calling to him. The past ending on 불렀습니다 places both actions in the past.
부르다 forms 불렀다 through the 르 irregular change and the past ending -었-. Minister Hong called to Gildong.
-습니다 presents the past action in the narrator's formal polite style.
이 marks 밤 as the subject: the night has gotten late.
-었- presents the night as having gotten late; the resulting late hour is relevant now.
-는데 gives the late hour as background for the father's question about why Gildong is still awake.
안 negates 자니. With 왜 아직, 안 자니 asks why Gildong is still not sleeping.
-니 ends a familiar informal question, used here by a father speaking to his child.
은 marks Gildong as the topic: he is the person who answered.
-했- places Gildong's answer in the past.
-습니다 ends the narration in a formal polite style.
이 marks the moon as the subject of 좋아서: the moon looked lovely.
-아서 gives the reason Gildong was looking at the moon: it was lovely. Past time comes from the final predicate.
-고 connects 보다 to the auxiliary 있다 here; together they express an ongoing action.
보고 있었습니다 describes looking at the moon as an action in progress at that past time.
-었- places the ongoing action in the past.
-습니다 makes Gildong's statement to his father formally polite.
들 explicitly marks more than one person.
은 introduces other people as the topic, contrasting them with Gildong.
중요한 describes the following noun 사람: important people.
The copula identifies the other people as important people.
입니다 ends Gildong's statement to his father in a formal, polite style.
는 sets up humble ‘I’ as the topic and contrasts Gildong with the other people mentioned previously.
-지 connects 그렇다, ‘be that way’, to the following negative auxiliary 않습니다. The written form retains ㅎ; ㅎ followed by ㅈ is pronounced as ㅊ, giving [그러치].
Gildong denies that he has the important standing that other people have: ‘I am not like that.’
-습니다 ends the negation in the formal polite style Gildong uses when addressing his father. 않습니다 is pronounced [안씀니다], while its written form remains unchanged.
도 adds Gildong to the category of people: ‘I am a person too.’
The copula connects the speaker to 사람: he is a person.
인데 presents his being a person as background that contrasts with his question about unequal treatment.
는 makes Gildong the contrasting topic: why is he different from other people?
들 marks multiple people, the others with whom Gildong compares himself.
과 marks the people used as the comparison with 다르다: ‘different from other people.’
-ㅂ니까 turns 다르다 into a formal polite question addressed to his father.
는 makes Minister Hong the topic: the sentence tells what he understood.
의 connects Gildong to 말: these are Gildong’s words.
을 marks Gildong’s words as what Minister Hong understood.
했 places Minister Hong’s understanding in the past.
습니다 gives the narrator’s statement a formal, polite ending.
도 adds concessive force to 그런데: ‘even so’. Minister Hong understood Gildong, yet still responded angrily.
를 marks 화 in the expression 화를 내다, meaning ‘get angry’ or ‘show anger’.
-며 connects expressing anger with asking: he asked while angry. The final verb supplies the past time.
묻다 changes its stem-final ㄷ to ㄹ before -었-, forming 물었다, ‘asked’. The past marker places his question before now.
The formal polite ending gives 물었습니다, ‘asked’, retaining the past tense in the narrator’s polite statement.
그게 contracts 그것이 and marks what Gildong just said as the subject of the question.
The copula connects 그게 to 말, referring to Gildong's statement.
-냐 makes this a plain, direct question. With 무슨, the father sternly asks, ‘What do you mean by that?’
이 marks Gildong as the person who spoke again.
-했- places Gildong's speaking in the past.
-습니다 gives the narrator's statement a formal polite ending.
는 marks polite 저 (‘I’) as the topic: Gildong is stating his relationship to his father.
의 connects 아버지 to 아들: Gildong is his father's son.
The copula connects ‘I’ with ‘Father's son’, stating Gildong's family relationship.
입니다 is the formal polite statement form of the copula, used as Gildong addresses his father respectfully.
와 joins Father and Mother as the two people Gildong is grateful to; the following 께 applies to both.
께 respectfully marks Mother, together with Father, as the people to whom Gildong expresses gratitude.
The ending -ㅂ니다 makes Gildong's statement of gratitude formal and polite.
는 marks the humble pronoun 저 as the topic: Gildong contrasts his own situation with what he wishes he could do.
를 marks his father as the person he cannot address by the quoted title.
라고 marks ‘아버지’ as the exact title used with 부르다: to call someone ‘Father’.
부르다 becomes 부를 before 수 to describe the action whose possibility is denied. 부를 is pronounced as written.
부를 수 없습니다 means that Gildong cannot call his father by this title because he is forbidden to do so.
없습니다 is the formal polite statement form of 없다, completing Gildong's respectful statement that this possibility is unavailable to him.
을 marks the older brother as the person Gildong cannot address by the quoted title.
이라고 marks ‘형’ as the title used when addressing the older brother.
부르다 becomes 부를 before 수 to express the possibility of calling someone something.
부를 수도 없습니다 says that calling his brother ‘Older Brother’ is also impossible; 도 adds this restriction to the preceding one.
도 adds this inability to the preceding inability: he cannot address his older brother as ‘Older Brother’ either.
없습니다 ends the statement of impossibility in a formal, polite style.
Gildong formally and politely tells his father that he is sad.
은 marks Gildong as the topic: the sentence tells what he did.
-었- places Gildong's crying in the past.
-습니다 ends the narration in a formal polite style.
도 means that Minister Hong also felt hurt, like Gildong.
이 marks 마음 as the subject. 마음이 아프다 expresses emotional pain: Minister Hong felt hurt.
아팠다 places Minister Hong's emotional pain in the past.
-습니다 ends the narrator's statement in a formal polite style.
에게 marks Gildong as the person to whom his father would speak.
좋은 describes 말을: kind words. 좋은 is pronounced [조은]: ㅎ is not pronounced before the vowel-initial ending, but remains in the written form.
말을 marks the words his father might say as the object.
해 connects 하다 to the auxiliary 주다. With 말을, 하다 means to say something.
주다 presents saying the words as an action done for Gildong; 면 makes this a condition.
grammar_links.display_meaning_en: if he says them for him

grammar_links.context_en: 주면 introduces the condition: if his father speaks kindly to Gildong.
이 marks Gildong as the person who might stop listening.
의 connects the father to his words or instructions.
말을 marks what Gildong might fail to heed. Listening to his father's words here means obeying him.
듣지 connects 듣다 to 않다, which supplies the negation.
않다 negates listening; the tentative ending makes this a possibility his father fears.
Here -을까 expresses an uncertain possibility that is the object of his father's worry: Gildong might not obey him.
The father's worry is narrated in the past.
Ends the narrator's statement in the formal polite style.
에게 marks Gildong as the person toward whom his father's anger is directed.
-게 makes 크다 an adverb describing how intensely his father showed anger.
를 marks 화 as the object in 화를 내다, meaning to get angry or show anger; here his father became angry with Gildong.
내다 takes the past form 내었다, contracted to 냈다. In 화를 내다, this means that he showed anger.
-습니다 ends the past statement in the narrator's formal polite style.
높은 describes the official post as high-ranking.
을 marks the official post as what the person holds in 벼슬을 하다.
하는 modifies 사람: a person who holds a high-ranking official post.
의 connects the official to his household, 집.
에서 identifies the household as where the woman works.
일하는 modifies 여자: a woman who works in the household.
의 identifies the sons as children of a woman who works in the household.
은 makes sons of household servants the topic; the father says Gildong is not the only such son.
만 restricts the claim to you alone. The following negation rejects that restriction: other sons are in the same situation.
있는 modifies the bound noun 것, presenting the situation of only Gildong existing in this category.
것이 아니다 negates the preceding situation, including the restriction expressed by 너만. The father says Gildong is not the only son of a woman working in such a household.
grammar_links.display_meaning_en: you are not the only one

grammar_links.context_en: 이 marks the nominalized situation as what 아니다 denies: it is not the case that Gildong is the only such son.
The father uses the plain statement form 아니다 while speaking directly to his son.
는 makes ‘you’ the topic: the father asks why Gildong says such things.
을 marks 말 as the object of 하다. Here 말을 하다 means to say something.
-느냐 ends a direct question in a plain, non-polite style. The father uses it to question his son sharply: ‘Why do you say such things?’
을 marks 말 as what Gildong might say again. 말을 하다 means to speak or say something.
-면 introduces the condition for the father's warning: if Gildong says such things again.
내 is the contraction of 나의, meaning 'my'; the father means in front of himself.
에 marks 앞 as the destination of coming: into the father's presence.
올 modifies 수 to present coming as a possible action.
올 수 없다 means 'cannot come.' In this warning, the father forbids Gildong from coming into his presence if he repeats these words.
The descriptive predicate 없다 ends in plain -다, giving the father's warning a firm, direct tone.
은 makes Gildong the topic: the sentence describes what he could not say.
도 emphasizes even a single word. With 아무 and the negative predicate, 아무 말도 means ‘not a single word’.
할 modifies 수. Here 말을 하다 means to say something, so 할 introduces the action whose possibility is denied.
할 수 없었습니다 expresses Gildong’s inability to speak; with 아무 말도, he could not say a single word.
The past form places Gildong’s inability to speak at this point in the story.
습니다 closes the narrator’s statement in a formal polite style.
에서 marks where Gildong continued crying: in front of his father.
The past ending places Gildong's crying in the narrated past.
-습니다 ends the narration in a formal polite style.
Minister Hong orders Gildong to go back. The stem 돌아가- combines with the plain command ending -아라; the adjacent 아 vowels merge in the written form 돌아가라.
의 identifies Minister Hong as the person whose words Gildong heard.
을 marks Minister Hong's words as what Gildong heard.
-고 connects hearing Minister Hong's words with returning to the room. The final past-tense verb places both actions in the past. 듣고 is pronounced 듣꼬: ㄱ becomes tense after the final ㄷ.
은 identifies Gildong as the person the statement is about.
으로 marks the room as the destination of Gildong's return.
-았- places Gildong's return in the past; 돌아가 plus -았- contracts to 돌아갔-. 돌아갔다 is pronounced 도라갇따: ㄹ links to the following vowel, final ㅆ sounds like ㄷ, and the following ㄷ becomes tense.

-습니다 presents Gildong's return in the narrator's formal polite style. 돌아갔습니다 is pronounced 도라갇씀니다: ㄹ links to the following vowel, final ㅆ sounds like ㄷ, the following ㅅ becomes tense, and ㅂ before ㄴ sounds like ㅁ.
에서 marks the room as the setting where Gildong continued to feel sad.
도 adds his room to the earlier setting: he remained sad there too after returning.
의 connects Gildong to 마음, identifying whose heart or feelings are described.
은 sets Gildong’s heart or feelings as the topic: he continued to feel sad.
슬펐- places his sadness in the past. The stem 슬프- loses ㅡ before the past ending, giving 슬펐-. The final ㅆ is pronounced as an unreleased ㄷ before the following consonant in both 슬펐다 and 슬펐습니다.
-습니다 finishes the narration in a formal polite style; 슬펐습니다 means ‘was sad’.

beats.event_en: Introduce Minister Hong, a respected official in Joseon, and his two sons: Inhyeong, born to his wife Lady Yu, and Gildong, born to the household servant Chunseom.
beats.quote: 화셜 됴션국 셰종됴 시졀의 ᄒᆞᆫ ᄌᆡ샹이 이시니 셩은 홍이오 명은 뫼라. ᄃᆡᄃᆡ 명문거죡으로 쇼년 등과ᄒᆞ여 벼ᄉᆞᆯ이 니죠판셔의 니르ᄆᆡ, 물망이 됴야의 읏듬이오, 츙효 겸비ᄒᆞ기로 일홈이 일국의 진동ᄒᆞ더라. 일즉 두 아들을 두어시니, 일ᄌᆞᄂᆞᆫ 일홈이 인형이니 뎡실 뉴시 쇼ᄉᆡᆼ이오, 일ᄌᆞᄂᆞᆫ 일홈이 길동이니 시비 츈셤의 쇼ᄉᆡᆼ이라.

beats.event_en: Chunseom becomes Minister Hong's concubine and gives birth to an extraordinary boy. Minister Hong is happy but regrets that the child was not born to his wife.
beats.quote: ᄒᆞ고, 언파의 손을 ᄯᅥᆯ치고 나가거ᄂᆞᆯ, 공이 가쟝 무류ᄒᆞ여 분긔ᄅᆞᆯ ᄎᆞᆷ지 못ᄒᆞ고 외당의 나와 부인의 지식이 업스물 한탄ᄒᆞ더니, 맛ᄎᆞᆷ 시비 츈셤이 ᄎᆞᄅᆞᆯ 올니긔로 그 고요ᄒᆞ믈 인ᄒᆞ여 츈셤을 잇글고 협실의 드러가 졍이 친압ᄒᆞ니, 이 ᄯᆡ 츈셤의 나히 십팔이라. ᄒᆞᆫ 번 몸을 허ᄒᆞᆫ 후로 문외의 나지 아니ᄒᆞ고 타인을 ᄎᆔᄒᆞᆯ ᄯᅳᆺ이 업스니, 공이 긔특이 넉여 인ᄒᆞ여 잉쳡을 삼아더니, 과연 그 달붓허 ᄐᆡ긔 잇셔 십 삭만의 일ᄀᆡ 옥동을 ᄉᆡᆼᄒᆞ니, 긔골이 비범ᄒᆞ여 진짓 영웅 호걸의 긔상이라. 공이 일변 깃거ᄒᆞ나 부인의게 나지 못ᄒᆞ믈 한ᄒᆞ더라.

beats.event_en: At eight, Gildong learns exceptionally quickly, and his father loves him increasingly. Nevertheless, because of his mother's low status, he is scolded for calling his father Father or his brother Brother. This restriction continues beyond age ten, and the servants' contempt deeply hurts him. One autumn night, he pushes aside his reading table and speaks.
beats.quote: 길동이 졈졈 ᄌᆞ라 팔 셰 되ᄆᆡ, 춍명이 과인ᄒᆞ여 ᄒᆞᆫ아흘 드르면 ᄇᆡᆨ을 통ᄒᆞ니 공이 더옥 ᄋᆡ즁ᄒᆞ나, 근본 쳔ᄉᆡᆼ이라 길동이 ᄆᆡ양 호부호형ᄒᆞ면 문득 ᄭᅮ지져 못ᄒᆞ계 ᄒᆞ니, 길동이 십 셰 넘도록 감히 부형을 부르지 못ᄒᆞ고, 비복 등이 쳔ᄃᆡᄒᆞ물 각골통한ᄒᆞ여 심ᄉᆞᄅᆞᆯ 졍치 못ᄒᆞ더니, 츄구월 망간을 당ᄒᆞᄆᆡ, 명월은 죠요ᄒᆞ고 쳥풍은 쇼슬ᄒᆞ여 사ᄅᆞᆷ의 심회ᄅᆞᆯ 돕ᄂᆞᆫ지라. 길동이 셔당의셔 글을 닑다가 문득 셔안을 밀치고 탄왈,

beats.event_en: Gildong wishes to accomplish great things for his country, but feels painfully alone because he cannot call his own father and brother by their family titles.
beats.quote: “대쟝뷔 셰샹의 나ᄆᆡ 공ᄆᆡᆼ을 본밧지 못ᄒᆞ면, 찰아리 병법을 외와 대쟝닌을 요하의 빗기 ᄎᆞ고 동졍셔벌ᄒᆞ여, 국가의 ᄃᆡ공을 셰우고 일홈을 만ᄃᆡ의 빗ᄂᆡ미 쟝부의 쾌ᄉᆡ라. 나ᄂᆞᆫ 엇지ᄒᆞ여 일신이 젹막ᄒᆞ고 부형이 이시되 호부호형을 못ᄒᆞ니 심쟝이 터질지라. 엇지 통한치 아니리오.”

beats.event_en: Gildong goes into the courtyard to practice swordsmanship. His father, who is also looking at the moon, notices him moving about and calls him over.
beats.quote: ᄒᆞ고, 말을 맛츠며 ᄯᅳᆯ의 나려 검술을 공부ᄒᆞ더니, 맛ᄎᆞᆷ 공이 ᄯᅩᄒᆞᆫ 월ᄉᆡᆨ을 구경ᄒᆞ다가 길동의 ᄇᆡ회ᄒᆞ믈 보고 즉시 불너 문왈,

beats.event_en: Minister Hong asks why Gildong is still awake so late.
beats.quote: “네 무ᄉᆞᆷ 흥이 이셔 야심토록 잠을 ᄌᆞ지 아니ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ다?”

beats.event_en: Gildong respectfully says that he enjoys the moonlight, but feels that he lacks the dignity other people possess.
beats.quote: “쇼인이 맛ᄎᆞᆷ 월ᄉᆡᆨ을 사랑ᄒᆞ미여니와, 대개 하ᄂᆞᆯ이 만물을 ᄂᆡ시ᄆᆡ 오직 사ᄅᆞᆷ이 귀ᄒᆞ오나, 쇼인의게 니ᄅᆞ러ᄂᆞᆫ 귀ᄒᆞ오미 업ᄉᆞ오니 엇지 사ᄅᆞᆷ이라 ᄒᆞ오리잇가.”

beats.event_en: Minister Hong understands what Gildong means but deliberately responds reproachfully.
beats.quote: 공이 그 말을 짐작ᄒᆞ나 짐즛 ᄎᆡᆨ왈,

beats.event_en: Minister Hong asks what Gildong means.
Gildong explains his sorrow directly: despite being his father's son and owing gratitude to his parents, he cannot call his father Father or his older brother Brother.
beats.quote: “쇼인이 평ᄉᆡᆼ 셜운 바ᄂᆞᆫ, 대감 졍긔로 당당ᄒᆞ온 남ᄌᆡ 되여ᄉᆞ오니 부ᄉᆡᆼ모휵지은이 깁ᄉᆞᆸ거ᄂᆞᆯ, 그 부친을 부친이라 못ᄒᆞ옵고, 그 형을 형이라 못ᄒᆞ오니 엇지 사ᄅᆞᆷ이라 ᄒᆞ오리잇가.”

beats.event_en: Gildong cries. His father feels sorry for him but fears that comforting him would encourage insolence, so he scolds him severely.
beats.quote: ᄒᆞ고, 눈물을 흘여 단삼을 젹시거ᄂᆞᆯ, 공니 쳥파의 비록 측은ᄒᆞ나 만일 그 ᄯᅳᆺ을 위로ᄒᆞ면 ᄆᆞᄅᆞᆷ이 방ᄌᆞᄒᆞᆯ가 져어 크게 ᄭᅮ지져 왈,

beats.event_en: Minister Hong says that Gildong is not the only child born to a low-status servant in an official's household and warns him never to raise this complaint again.
beats.quote: “ᄌᆡ샹가 쳔비 쇼ᄉᆡᆼ이 비단 너ᄲᅮᆫ이 아니거든, 네 엇지 방ᄌᆞᄒᆞ미 이 ᄀᆞᆺ흐뇨. ᄎᆞ후 다시 이런 말이 이시면 안젼의 용납지 못ᄒᆞ리라.”

beats.event_en: Gildong cannot answer and continues crying while bowed to the ground. His father sends him away, and he returns to his room still grieving.
beats.quote: ᄒᆞ니, 길동이 감이 일언을 고치 못ᄒᆞ고 다만 복지유쳬 ᄲᅮᆫ이라. 공이 명ᄒᆞ여 물너가라 하거ᄂᆞᆯ, 길동이 침쇼로 도라와 슬허ᄒᆞ믈 마지 아이ᄒᆞ더라.

entries.role_en: Father of Hong Inhyeong and Hong Gildong. A high-ranking official whose wife is Lady Yu; Chunseom, initially a household servant, becomes his concubine. He loves Gildong but forbids him to address him as Father.
Minister Hong and Chunseom's son, and Hong Inhyeong's younger half-brother. He learns exceptionally quickly but suffers unequal treatment because of his mother's low status.
Minister Hong and Lady Yu's son, and Hong Gildong's older half-brother. Gildong is forbidden to address him as Brother.
Minister Hong's wife and Hong Inhyeong's mother; she is distinct from Chunseom, Gildong's mother.
Hong Gildong's mother. Initially a servant in Minister Hong's household, she becomes his concubine. Her low social status underlies Gildong's unequal treatment.

The single essential historical vocabulary exemption: Minister Hong's government position establishes the household's high standing, contrasting with Chunseom's low status and the restrictions imposed on their son.
